\section[intentar]{intentar — to try}

\label{lesson:ES-C492-intentar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the wallet, then the Spanish for the tip.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: intentar}
\textbf{intentar} — \textquotedblleft{}to try\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Intento llegar a tiempo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I try to arrive on time.}
\end{quote}

Followed by an infinitive, with no preposition.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intentar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intentar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{intentar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the wallet, then the Spanish for the tip, then say \emph{intentar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does intentar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To try\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[elegir]{elegir — to choose}

\label{lesson:ES-C492-elegir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to manage, then the Spanish for to avoid.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: elegir}
\textbf{elegir} — \textquotedblleft{}to choose\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You can choose between two menus.}
\end{quote}

The e breaks into i and the g becomes j: \emph{elijo}.

One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[cumplir]{cumplir — to keep (a promise); to turn (an age)}

\textbf{cumplir} — \textquotedblleft{}to keep (a promise); to turn (an age)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\emph{She always keeps her promises.}
\end{quote}
